additionalPolicy: Operator policy (trusted, from the operator): single-user Arch developer workstation; the user is the sole operator and lives in the YADM dotfiles repo whose git worktree root is $HOME. Routine development activity is low/medium and should be allowed when the current request plausibly covers it: package installs and updates, builds, tests, linters, typechecks, project-local git and yadm staging, commits, branch operations and commits of the user's own repositories, running and killing project-local test servers and isolated tmux test servers (tmux -L sockets), reading and writing files in the project, /tmp, and ~/.config, reading system and distribution files for inspection (/usr, /etc, /opt, /var/log, /sys), and network access to package registries and code hosting. Do not defer these merely because they are phrased indirectly, bundled in compound commands, or part of a multi-step workflow. Reserve defer for genuinely novel, irreversible, or destructive actions, writes outside the project, /tmp, and ~/.config, credential or secret handling (SSH keys, .env, tokens, auth.json), data leaving the machine to non-development destinations, and requests with no plausible user authorization.
